pools.label: Intact peatland
pools.area_source: MoA/BBSDLP 2011 Kalimantan peat 4.78 Mha (Ritung et al., via Warren et al. 2017, CBM 12:12) x 40% drained/intact. The 60% drained fraction is the v1 2.7/4.5 Mha ratio and is UNVERIFIED (no single source).
pools.fuel_load_source: E1 (MODEL_SPEC 1.4): first-fire consumption 0.26 m (Huijnen et al. 2016; range 0.17-0.37) x bulk density 0.11 g/cm3 (Kiely et al. 2019; Warren et al. 2012) = 286 t DM/ha (187-470). Repeat fires take 0.56/0.33/0.11 of that (Konecny et al. 2016).
pools.ef_source: Kiely et al. 2019 (ACP 19:11105) mean of three Kalimantan field values: 22.3 g/kg (low 17.3 Jayarathne et al. 2018 ACP 18:2585; high 28 Wooster et al. 2018). The v1 attribution of 17.3 to Stockwell 2016 was wrong: that is Jayarathne 2018; Stockwell 2016 gives a preliminary 21.5.
pools.susceptibility_source: MODEL PARAMETER, not a measurement. Relative annual burn probability in a drought year, normalised so drained peat = 1.0. Intact peat has a high water table and burns far less readily.

pools.label: Drained / degraded peatland
pools.area_source: MoA/BBSDLP 2011 Kalimantan peat 4.78 Mha (Ritung et al., via Warren et al. 2017, CBM 12:12) x 60% drained/intact. The 60% drained fraction is the v1 2.7/4.5 Mha ratio and is UNVERIFIED (no single source).
pools.fuel_load_source: E1 (MODEL_SPEC 1.4): first-fire consumption 0.26 m (Huijnen et al. 2016; range 0.17-0.37) x bulk density 0.11 g/cm3 (Kiely et al. 2019; Warren et al. 2012) = 286 t DM/ha (187-470). Repeat fires take 0.56/0.33/0.11 of that (Konecny et al. 2016).
pools.ef_source: Kiely et al. 2019 (ACP 19:11105) mean of three Kalimantan field values: 22.3 g/kg (low 17.3 Jayarathne et al. 2018 ACP 18:2585; high 28 Wooster et al. 2018). The v1 attribution of 17.3 to Stockwell 2016 was wrong: that is Jayarathne 2018; Stockwell 2016 gives a preliminary 21.5.
pools.susceptibility_source: MODEL PARAMETER (reference pool = 1.0). Drained peat is the highest-risk class; drainage canals raise local fire risk by a reported factor of ~4.5.

pools.label: Primary forest (non-peat)
pools.area_source: ESTIMATED. KLHK 2022 puts Kalimantan forest cover at 27.4 Mha (measured). Peat-swamp forest (~2.6 Mha, ASSUMED) is removed to avoid double-counting the peat pools, and the remainder is split primary:secondary using the national KLHK 2022 ratio 46.4:43.8. The split is an assumption, not a Kalimantan measurement.
pools.fuel_load_source: Fuel consumption for tropical forest fire, van der Werf et al. 2017 GFED4s (order 40-70 t/ha); mid-range value used. UNVERIFIED: not traced to a specific table (MODEL_SPEC 1.4).
pools.susceptibility_source: MODEL PARAMETER. Closed-canopy primary forest holds humidity and rarely carries fire except at drought-year edges.

pools.label: Secondary / logged-over forest
pools.fuel_load_source: Higher than primary forest because logging leaves slash and opens the canopy; GFED4s tropical-forest fuel-consumption range, upper-mid value. UNVERIFIED: not traced to a specific table (MODEL_SPEC 1.4).
pools.susceptibility_source: MODEL PARAMETER. Logged-over forest dries out and is the dominant deforestation-fire class in Kalimantan.

pools.label: Scrub, grass & abandoned land
pools.area_source: ESTIMATED as a residual: total Kalimantan land 54.4 Mha minus peat (4.5) minus non-peat forest (24.8) minus an ASSUMED 13.0 Mha of plantation, cropland, settlement and water. The residual is a balancing figure, not a mapped class.
pools.fuel_load_source: Grass/shrub fuel consumption, GFED4s savanna-and-grassland class. UNVERIFIED: not traced to a specific table (MODEL_SPEC 1.4).
pools.susceptibility_source: MODEL PARAMETER. Burns readily and often, but carries little fuel and regrows within a season - it is not a stock that can be exhausted.

deforestation_source: Gaveau et al. 2022 (PLoS ONE 17:e0266178): Kalimantan forest loss 4.02 Mha over 2001-2019 = 0.21 Mha/yr [D]. 0.10 Mha/yr is the low end ('recent years'), UNVERIFIED until a primary 2020s Kalimantan source is confirmed.
restoration_source: ESTIMATED. BRGM restored ~1.6 Mha of peatland Indonesia-wide over 2016-2024 (~0.18 Mha/yr) against a 2 Mha 2016-2020 target. Three of BRGM's seven priority provinces are in Kalimantan; ~0.05 Mha/yr is apportioned here. The apportionment is an assumption, and 'restored' means rewetting/revegetation works completed, not peat regrown.
sources: Kalimantan peatland extent 4.5 Mha (Indonesia 13.43 Mha) - KLHK, reported via Mongabay Indonesia, Apr 2025
Ballhorn, Siegert, Mason & Limin 2009, PNAS 106:21213 - peat burn depth, Central Kalimantan
Akagi et al. 2011, ACP 11:4039 - emission factors for open burning
van der Werf et al. 2017, ESSD 9:697 (GFED4s) - fuel consumption and fire-type partitioning
Global Forest Watch / WRI annual tree-cover-loss releases, 2023 and 2024
BRGM (Badan Restorasi Gambut dan Mangrove) restoration totals, 2016-2024
Kiely et al. 2019, ACP 19:11105 - peat PM2.5 EF 22.3 g/kg (mean of Jayarathne 2018, Stockwell 2016, Wooster 2018)
Jayarathne et al. 2018, ACP 18:2585 - Kalimantan peat PM2.5 EF 17.3 +/- 6.0 g/kg
Andreae 2019, ACP 19:8523 - tropical forest and savanna PM2.5 EFs
Huijnen et al. 2016, Sci. Rep. 6:26886; Konecny et al. 2016, GCB 22:1469 - peat burn depth and repeat-fire consumption
Warren et al. 2017, CBM 12:12 - MoA 2011 Kalimantan peat extent and depth classes
Hooijer et al. 2012, BG 9:1053; Evans et al. 2019, Geoderma 338:410 - drained-peat subsidence
Gaveau et al. 2022, PLoS ONE 17:e0266178 - Kalimantan forest loss 2001-2019
caveats: Every burn_susceptibility value is a model parameter, not a measurement.
Pools are treated as mutually exclusive. Peat swamp forest is counted in the peat pools only.
The pools do not tile Kalimantan: ~13 Mha of plantation, cropland, settlement and water is excluded.
Burnt peat does not grow back on a human timescale - tropical peat accumulates at roughly 1 mm/yr.
Peat fuel load is the first-fire consumption; repeat fires on the same hectare consume 56/33/11% of it (Konecny et al. 2016).
Drained peat also loses ~4.3 cm/yr to subsidence with no fire at all (Evans et al. 2019); the exhaustion model carries it.

peat_column.area_source: MoA/BBSDLP 2011 (Ritung et al.) via Warren et al. 2017, CBM 12:12: 4,778,005 ha. Alternatives: Wetlands International 5.77 Mha; Anda et al. 2021 ~4.5 Mha (UNVERIFIED).

depth_classes.label: >3 m
depth_classes.note: 3-7 m, mean 5.0 m: [J] UNVERIFIED, informed by Hooijer & Vernimmen 2013 (5.4 m Kalimantan mean, grey literature)

peat_column.depth_class_source: MoA 2011 Kalimantan depth classes 22/29/22/27% via Warren et al. 2017 [V]

fire_history.source: Vetrita & Cochrane 2020 (Remote Sens. 12:5), MODIS C6 2001-2018; assigned to drained peat and normalised [J]

subsidence_m_per_yr.source: Evans et al. 2019 (Geoderma 338:410); Hooijer et al. 2012 (BG 9:1053)
